subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was fired and handed the solved murder case of Janussi, with the understanding that he would save face and receive the promised reward for cracking it.
source_quote: Alright. I think we just hand it to him — let him save face, since he got fired — with the understanding that they make good on the promise: we get our reward for helping crack the case.

subject: Alkrist
fact: Alkrist confessed under Kalan's Zone of Truth spell to killing Janussi, providing the conclusive piece of evidence in the murder mystery.
source_quote: Alkrist had said it out loud, in the room, with Kalan's spell still holding him honest — he'd killed Janussi.

subject: Ember Vanguard
fact: The Ember Vanguard is a rival faction that has become infamous underground, with exaggerated rumors and posters bearing the group's name, overshadowing the party's actual deeds.
source_quote: The Ember Vanguard, running ahead of us in every rumor, bigger and meaner than the four of us in a room arguing about a dead sage.

subject: reward claim
fact: The party has an unresolved claim for a promised reward tied to solving Janussi’s murder, contingent on Kalan Strongbranch’s official acknowledgment.
source_quote: with the understanding that they make good on the promise: we get our reward for helping crack the case.

subject: Dawnbringer's therapy
fact: Dawnbringer insists on continuing therapeutic sessions, believing the first session was productive, and the party owes her this due to prior commitments made on her behalf.
source_quote: I'm not leaving here without the therapy. That first session was actually very productive. I really feel we need to—

subject: infamy vs. anonymity
fact: The party is divided on whether to leverage their fame for recognition or remain hidden, given their existing notoriety in underground circles.
source_quote: We're already infamous underground. It didn't seem to serve us well.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is the destination where the party sought answers and unresolved questions from various scholars and keepers, including those related to Dawnbringer’s therapy and Janussi’s murder.
source_quote: the things we came to Candlekeep to ask the various folks, questions still owed to us.

subject: Zone of Truth
fact: Kalan’s Zone of Truth spell was active during Alkrist’s confession, ensuring the veracity of the admission and serving as the catalyst for resolving the murder mystery.
source_quote: with Kalan's spell still holding him honest

subject: sword whisperer
fact: The party has been searching for a sword whisperer — a specialist who understands the psychological toll on blades — for Dawnbringer, who is built to carry such a weapon.
source_quote: I'd been the one hunting a sword whisperer for her since the road south — months where the thing she was built to carry just wasn't there

subject: Alkrist's confession
fact: Alkrist publicly confessed to murdering Janussi under magical compulsion, ending the investigation and shifting responsibility to Kalan Strongbranch.
source_quote: Alkrist had said it out loud, in the room, with Kalan's spell still holding him honest — he'd killed Janussi.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient entity who communicates telepathically, seeks therapeutic intervention for blade-related trauma, and is identified by the party as female despite uncertainty about her nature.
source_quote: She could make noises in my head... I thought Dawnbringer was a she... Whatever — she. Yeah, I think we said she.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the de facto leader of the party in this scene, proposing the resolution to hand the case to Kalan, advocating for reward fulfillment, and mediating discussions on infamy.
source_quote: Alright. I think we just hand it to him — let him save face, since he got fired — with the understanding that they make good on the promise...

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir challenges assumptions about infamy and the party’s public perception, noting their existing notoriety and the misrepresentation by the Ember Vanguard.
source_quote: We're already infamous underground. It didn't seem to serve us well.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz provides a pragmatic fallback plan of violent escalation — hacking and slashing — as a contingency when diplomatic or strategic options fail.
source_quote: If things go sideways, we can always start hacking and slashing.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: Gracklstugh is a location where the party is wanted on posters bearing their name, contributing to their underground infamy despite being misrepresented.
source_quote: Gracklstugh still had our name on posters, wrong enough to be cover but our name all the same.

subject: Kalan's firing
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was dismissed from his position prior to solving Janussi’s murder, making the resolution of the case both a redemption and an ironic twist.
source_quote: Kalan had gotten fired. That's the terrain — a man told he was done, standing next to a case he couldn't crack, that we cracked for him.

subject: Bookwyrm's justice
fact: A potential path to justice remains open through Bookwyrm, though the party chose to defer to Kalan instead, leaving this option unresolved.
source_quote: Or we could walk straight to Bookwyrm and demand justice and satisfaction.

subject: A'lai's involvement
fact: A thread connects the murder to A'lai, suggesting deeper political or personal stakes, but the party chose not to pursue him directly.
source_quote: we knew there was a thread running from all this back to A'lai.

subject: Dawnbringer's telepathy
fact: Dawnbringer demonstrated the ability to communicate telepathically with the narrator, producing a distinct mental sound like a palm slapping stone, confirming her non-human nature.
source_quote: a click inside my skull, a sound like a palm slapping stone, whatever that was supposed to mean.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is an observer and recorder of events, documenting the party’s decisions without leading them, emphasizing the act of witnessing over action.
source_quote: I don't lead these conversations. I record them, and I watch who's pretending.
